claims.statement: Every library mutation exists exactly once, as a subcommand module's `pub async fn main(&mut SqliteConnection, &ArgMatches, &ProgressBar)`. The GraphQL host reaches it through `spawn_cli_action` in `src/mutation.rs` and the MCP host through `run_action` in `src/mcp/actions.rs`, each building an argv vec and parsing it with the module's own `subcommand().try_get_matches_from(...)` before calling that module's `main()`, so CLI, GraphQL and MCP share one implementation per action.

The system is layered by call direction: a clap entrypoint (`src/main.rs`) dispatches to one module per user-facing action; those modules sit on shared layers — `database.rs` (every SQL statement as a standalone `pub async fn` taking `&mut SqliteConnection`), `model.rs` (row types, int-encoded enums, Logiqx XML types), `common.rs` (`CommonRomfile` plus the format-abstraction traits), `config.rs`, `util.rs`, `mimetype.rs`, `progress.rs`, `prompt.rs`, `transcode.rs` — which in turn use the format modules, and every codec a format module drives now runs in-process (a `crates/*` member, sevenz-rust2/zip, or nod) except the single `ctrtool` subprocess. The data lands in one SQLite file.

`src/main.rs` runs batch subcommands inside a block that holds the single pooled connection, then dispatches `mcp::main(pool.clone(), ...)` and `server::main(pool.clone(), ...)` outside that block because those hosts multiplex requests, and finally calls `optimize_database(pool)` — which itself needs a connection.

`establish_connection` chooses the SQLite pool shape from the Cargo feature set with `cfg_if`: `server` or `mcp` compiled in gives `max_connections = 5` with `PRAGMA locking_mode = NORMAL`, otherwise one connection with `EXCLUSIVE`. It then applies WAL, `synchronous = NORMAL`, `temp_store`, `mmap_size`, `cache_size`, `auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL`, `foreign_keys = ON`, and runs the compile-time-embedded `MIGRATOR`.

Cargo features remove whole modules rather than hiding routes: `src/main.rs` declares `mod mcp`, `mod mutation`, `mod query`, `mod server` and `mod validator` under `#[cfg(feature = ...)]`, so a default build never compiles the HTTP or MCP stack. `#[cfg_attr(feature = "server", derive(... SimpleObject))]` on the `model.rs` row types lets the same structs serve GraphQL without a parallel type set.

`spawn_cli_action` returns immediately: it spawns a task that emits `{prefix}_started` over SSE, acquires its own pooled connection (reporting an acquire failure as `{prefix}_error` instead of panicking), runs the subcommand closure, then emits `{prefix}_complete` or `{prefix}_error`. The mutation resolver itself returns `true` as soon as the work is handed off.

`OxyromonMcp::run_action` drives the shared subcommand synchronously: it takes the process-wide `write_lock` (one lock per stdio process, and one shared by every per-request HTTP handler) for the whole action so SQLite writer serialization is ordered rather than surfacing as SQLITE_BUSY, acquires one pooled connection, creates a hidden progress bar that a poller samples about every 400 ms into `notifications/progress`, and races the work against the per-request and server-shutdown cancellation tokens. Read tools take no lock, and `--read-only` disables the write routes so they never appear in `tools/list`.

`server::main` builds one axum `Router` owning `POST /graphql`, `GET /events` (SSE), multipart `POST /dats`, `/roms`, `/patches`, `/irds`, `GET /romfiles/{id}`, the nested `/mcp` Streamable HTTP service, and the embedded SPA served from `target/assets` by `rust-embed`; MCP therefore shares the listener and the caller's trust level with `/graphql`.

When the MCP server is mounted by `server.rs` its mutating actions fan their start/complete/error outcomes into the same SSE broadcast channel, so a browser watching `/events` reacts to work started over MCP; the standalone stdio server has `sse_tx: None` and emits nothing.

HTTP uploads do not implement their own import: the handlers stream the multipart body to a temp directory, then drive `import_roms::main` / `import_irds::main` with synthesized argv or `import_dats`'s `process_dat_upload` helper on a spawned task, keeping the temp directory alive until the import finishes and reporting over SSE.

Because argv is the interchange format, non-CLI hosts must supply the answers a human would give at a prompt: `-y`/`--yes` for destructive confirmations, `-u`/`--unattended` for ambiguous ROM matches, `--system <name>` to bypass the system multiselect. Where argv is the wrong shape the host calls the module's exported helper directly instead of forking an implementation (`purge_systems::purge_system`, `download_dats::download_redump_systems`).

The Cargo workspace members are the root `oxyromon` package plus `crates/*` (`gdi-rs`, `nsz-rs`, `xdelta-rs`, `xps-rs`, `xso-rs`), depended on by `path` + `version` with `default-features = false`. `frontend/` and `desktop/` are not members: each declares its own `[workspace]` table so cargo does not walk up to the root package, keeping the WebAssembly and Tauri/webview dependency trees out of the native build.

`build.rs` runs `trunk build --release` inside `frontend/` when the `server` feature is enabled (skipped by `SKIP_TRUNK=true`, with an explicit assertion when `frontend/` is absent from a published crate) and always creates `target/assets` so the `rust-embed` folder exists at compile time.

The Tauri desktop shell adds no backend layer: it reserves a free loopback port, spawns the same `oxyromon` binary as a sidecar running `server --address 127.0.0.1 --port <port>`, polls the port until it accepts connections, and points the webview at it.

`romfiles.path` is stored relative to the `ROM_DIRECTORY` setting: `CommonFile::get_relative_path` strips the directory before a path is persisted, and the server's `download_romfile` handler joins the stored relative path back onto the `ROM_DIRECTORY` setting to open the file.

Under `oxyromon mcp` (or `/mcp`) stdout is the MCP JSON-RPC channel, so nothing on a reachable code path may `println!` there; all user-facing output goes through the categorized `print_*` helpers in `progress.rs`, which write via the global `MultiProgress`, and `log::*` records are bridged onto the same UI in `main.rs`.

CPU-bound codec work is kept off the async runtime: `run_blocking` runs a synchronous format-crate entry point on `spawn_blocking`, resets the shared bar to a bytes style with the input size as its length, and feeds the crate's `&mut dyn FnMut(u64)` progress callback into it; modules with a different shape (archive listing, nod disc writing, opening a CHD header) call `spawn_blocking` directly. There is no generic external-tool runner left: `ctrtool` spawns `tokio::process::Command` itself and bails with captured stderr, and `util::tool_version` is the only remaining helper that shells out, returning `unknown` rather than failing when its regex does not match.

Format modules share one availability contract: in-process codecs return `"built-in"` from `get_version()` (`nsz.rs` appends `prod.keys not found` so the missing key file is not first discovered mid-compression), while `ctrtool` alone parses the tool's version output via `tool_version`. `info::main`, the GraphQL `dependencies` query and the MCP `status` payload all walk the same eight-entry set (`sevenz-rust2`, `chd-rs`, `ctrtool`, `xps-rs`, `xso-rs`, `nsz-rs`, `xdelta-rs`, `nod` for RVZ/WBFS), so only `ctrtool` can be reported missing; `import_roms` probes it before a CIA import and reports `Required tool not found: ctrtool` instead of failing deeper.

Subcommand tests drive the same entry points the servers do: a temp database from `establish_connection`, ROM/tmp settings pointed at `TempDir`s, argv parsed by the module's own `subcommand()`, a call to `main(&mut connection, &matches, &ProgressBar::hidden())`, and assertions on database plus filesystem state, with the `cfg(test)`-only `MUTEX` in `config.rs` serializing tests that share process-wide state.

Settings live in a key/value table with two scopes: `config::get_setting` prefers the row carrying the requested `system_id` and falls back to the global row, and `get_rom_directory` / `get_tmp_directory` persist a first-run default (`OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY` or `~/Emulation`; `OXYROMON_TMP_DIRECTORY` or the system temp dir) the first time they are read, which is why the entrypoint calls them for their side effect.

`src/transcode.rs` is the single decode layer between stored romfiles and neutral-format work. Every helper returns `Decoded<T> { source, inner }`: `source` is the romfile as the database knows it (the path and size a conversion commits against) and `inner` is the same content in a neutral format (`CommonRomfile`, `IsoRomfile`, `CueBinRomfile`, `NspRomfile`) written into the caller's `TempDir`. `archive_to_common`, `common_as_source`, `xso_to_iso`, `nsz_to_nsp`, `rvz_to_iso`, `archive_to_cue_bin` and `assemble_cue_bin` cover the containers, and callers in `convert_roms`/`export_roms` consume `decoded.source` when persisting, so the tmp decode is never mistaken for the library file.

CHD decoding and creation run in-process through the `chd-rs` crate rather than a chdman subprocess: `chd.rs` reads headers with `Chd::open`/`Chd::open_with_parent` on `spawn_blocking`, and drives `chd_rs::create_cd`/`create_dvd`/`create_hd`/`create_ld` and `extract_cd`/`extract_ld`/`Chd::extract` through `run_blocking`, reproducing chdman's own default codec lists and hunk sizes when the user gives none. Only `ctrtool` remains an external executable, so a CHD conversion needs nothing installed on `PATH`.

Parent-CHD resolution lives in one shared function: `transcode::romfile_as_chd` follows `romfile.parent_id` through `find_romfile_by_id` and calls `as_chd_with_parent` (which verifies the parent's SHA1 against the child's recorded `parent_sha1`), falling back to plain `as_chd`. `check_roms`, `convert_roms` and `export_roms` all route CHD access through it, and `chd_to_iso` layers the DVD-specific decode on top, returning `Ok(None)` for a non-DVD CHD so a caller skips the chain instead of branching on `ChdType` itself.

`util.rs` owns two invariants the mutation subcommands depend on rather than reimplementing: `get_kept_directories` (the ROM, system and `Trash` directories that must never be removed) paired with `remove_empty_directories`, which climbs from a deleted file's directory up to a kept or non-empty directory and stops rather than recursing; and `compute_system_completion`, which recomputes game and system completion (creating placeholder files for empty missing ROMs, with arcade systems routed by merging mode) and is called by `import_dats`, `import_roms`, `import_irds`, `sort_roms`, `check_roms`, `rebuild_roms`, `purge_roms` and `purge_irds`.
